intro: Lesson 6: Akbar and Jahangir: ruling a vast and diverse empire. To understand how Akbar and Jahangir ruled a large and diverse empire

questions.q: Explain how the mansabdar system helped Akbar control the empire.
questions.a: Officials held ranks from the emperor and supplied soldiers; ranks could be changed, so they stayed loyal
questions.model: Point: the mansabdar system kept nobles loyal. Evidence: ranks and income came from Akbar and could be taken away. Explain: so nobles depended on him and supplied soldiers.

questions.q: Why did ending the jizya matter to many subjects?
questions.a: Most were Hindu, so it removed a tax and won their loyalty
The English ambassador to Jahangir's court from 1615

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box, write two PEEL paragraphs: 'How did Akbar keep control of a vast and diverse empire?'
questions.a: Paragraphs on administration (mansabdars, Todar Mal's tax) and on including different groups (ending the jizya, Rajput nobles)
questions.model: Teacher goes through paragraph 1: 'Akbar kept control through his administration (P). Mansabdars held ranks given by him (E). They depended on him for income, so they stayed loyal (E). This helped him rule a huge area (L).'

questions.q: Extend: Why did many scholars criticise Akbar's religious ideas?
questions.a: They saw his new religious ideas as going against the teachings of Islam

questions.q: Stretch: Was Akbar a successful ruler? Give a balanced judgement.
questions.a: Successful in administration and keeping peace; criticised for religious ideas that went against Islam

questions.q: Big question: how do you rule millions of people of different faiths?
questions.a: With strong administration, fair taxes, loyal officials and including different groups, while staying true to your principles
